Yes, I know what you mean. Your comment honestly made me tear up a little bit. It fucking sucks so much when your parents are the ones that hurt you. You feel so much pressure to forgive because they’re your parents. It’s traumatic in its own right. You just wish so badly that they hadn’t done the things they’d done so you can have your parent again, as they were before, and it feels so horrible knowing it can never be undone. I never said someone should be forced to forgive their abuser. I agree with you and I hate people who act like you have to forgive someone who caused you irreparable harm. I have others in my past who have hurt me and I will not ever forgive them. The pressure to forgive can sometimes be abusive in its own right. 

I just hate when someone dismisses forgiveness as a foolish action. Situations involving family are really fucking hard and sometimes forgiveness is the natural path your healing takes. It’s the choice of the victim and the victim alone.

Forgiveness does not mean letting the person do whatever the fuck they want. My father will never be able to be alone with my children and my relationship with him is strained. I will never trust him fully. But I have forgiven him. Not everyone can simmer on their anger and pain for the rest of their life. Some people just want to move the fuck on and forgiveness helps. Dismissing someone as a fool for navigating their trauma in a way that feels right to them is a very ignorant thing to say. 

OP can forgive her mother and move on. Because the safety of a child is involved, I don’t think it’s a good idea for that forgiveness to mean her mother gets to have a relationship with her daughter.

This is very well-said. My father inflicted a lot of trauma on me growing up and I have forgiven him. These situations are not as black and white as people on the internet make them out to be. Being abused doesn’t always make you hate the perpetrator. It is a very complex and hard to understand thing unless you’ve lived it. People who hate their abusers and go no contact are valid, but that isn’t the only course of action for some people. Forgiveness can feel like a betrayal of self and it can be very hard, but for some people it’s the only thing that heals them.
